entities.summary: Porto, officially the Ancient, Very Noble, Ever Loyal and Undefeated City of Porto, is the second largest city in Portugal, after Lisbon. It is the capital of the Porto District and one of the Iberian Peninsula's major urban areas. Porto city proper, which is the entire municipality of Porto, is small compared to its metropolitan area, with an estimated population of 252,687 people in a municipal area of 41.42 km2 (16 sq mi). As of 2025, the Porto metropolitan area is projected to reach 1.2 million inhabitants. Porto's strategic location on the Douro River has made it a crucial hub for trade and commerce since the Roman era, earning it the nickname 'Cidade do Fino Vinho' (City of Fine Wine). The city's rich history is reflected in its well-preserved Romanesque architecture, picturesque riverside quarter, and stunning cathedral, Porto Cathedral. Porto's cultural significance extends beyond its impressive landmarks, as it has been a center for artistic and literary innovation, with famous writers and poets such as Luís de Camões and Fernando Pessoa calling the city home. Porto's transformation into a major urban center was fueled by the arrival of the Portuguese Age of Discovery, which brought significant economic growth and cultural exchange. The city's unique blend of medieval and modern architecture, combined with its vibrant cultural scene, has made Porto a popular destination for tourists and a hub for international business and innovation.
